title: Dimension formula for a closed dominant morphism
statement:
Let $f:V\to U$ be a dominant morphism locally of finite type between integral schemes, and assume $U$ is locally Noetherian. Write $k(U)$ and $k(V)$ for the residue fields of their generic points (their function fields), with the injection $k(U)\hookrightarrow k(V)$ induced by $f$, and let $r=\operatorname{trdeg}_{k(U)}k(V)$. Then $\dim V\leq\dim U+r$. If the underlying continuous map of $f$ is closed, then $\dim V=\dim U+r$. Dimension is topological Krull dimension, allowing infinity. In particular, for a proper such $f$ inducing a finite extension of function fields, $\dim V=\dim U$.

The notions use [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [pqf-def-locnoeth], [def-sc-function-field], [def-kun-transcendence-degree], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and [def-weil-proper-morphism]; a closed map sends every closed subset to a closed subset.

source.place: Tag 02JX, lemma-alteration-dimension; the final specialization uses that proper maps are closed and a finite field extension has transcendence degree zero.
